title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 24 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 24 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 24 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 24.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 24, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Joash repaired the house of the LORD
A chest was made for collecting money
questions.explanation: Joash began to reign at seven years old, which is stated in 2 Chronicles 24:1.

questions.question: How old was Joash when he began to reign?
questions.explanation: The text states that Joash was seven years old when he began to reign (2 Chronicles 24:1).

questions.question: Who was Joash's mother?
questions.explanation: Joash's mother's name is Zibiah, as stated in 2 Chronicles 24:1.

questions.question: Who did Joash do right in the sight of?
questions.explanation: Joash did that which was right in the sight of the LORD all the days of Jehoiada the priest (2 Chronicles 24:2).

questions.question: What did Jehoiada take for Joash?
questions.explanation: Jehoiada took for Joash two wives, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 24:3.

questions.question: What did Joash decide to repair?
questions.explanation: Joash was minded to repair the house of the LORD (2 Chronicles 24:4).

questions.question: Who did Joash gather together to collect money?
questions.explanation: Joash gathered together the priests and the Levites to collect money (2 Chronicles 24:5).

questions.question: What collection did Joash refer to when speaking to Jehoiada?
options: The collection according to the commandment of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: The collection according to the commandment of Moses
questions.explanation: Joash referred to the collection according to the commandment of Moses when speaking to Jehoiada (2 Chronicles 24:6).

questions.question: Who had broken up the house of God?
questions.explanation: The sons of Athaliah had broken up the house of God (2 Chronicles 24:7).

questions.question: What did they make at the king's commandment?
questions.explanation: At the king's commandment, they made a chest (2 Chronicles 24:8).

questions.question: What was proclaimed through Judah and Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: They made a proclamation to bring in to the LORD the collection (2 Chronicles 24:9).

questions.question: True or False: Joash reigned for forty years in Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Joash reigned for forty years in Jerusalem, as stated in 2 Chronicles 24:1.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoiada was a priest during Joash's reign.
questions.explanation: Jehoiada was indeed a priest during Joash's reign, as indicated in 2 Chronicles 24:2.

questions.question: True or False: Joash had only one wife.
questions.explanation: Joash had two wives, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 24:3.

questions.question: True or False: The Levites were quick to gather the money for the temple repair.
questions.explanation: The Levites hastened it not, according to 2 Chronicles 24:5.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 24 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 24 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the princes and people do with the chest according to 2 Chronicles 24:10?
options: They rejoiced and cast into the chest
questions.correctAnswer: They rejoiced and cast into the chest
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as it directly reflects the action described in 2 Chronicles 24:10, where the princes and people brought in and cast into the chest until they had made an end.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 24:11 promise will happen if someone brings money into the chest?
questions.explanation: This is affirmed in 2 Chronicles 24:11, where it states that the king's scribe and the high priest's officer came and emptied the chest, gathering money in abundance.

questions.question: Who did the king and Jehoiada give the collected money to for the repair of the house of the LORD?
options: Those who did the work of the service
questions.correctAnswer: Those who did the work of the service
questions.explanation: According to 2 Chronicles 24:12, the king and Jehoiada gave the money to those who did the work of the service of the house of the LORD.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 24:13 indicate about the workmen's performance?
questions.explanation: The statement in 2 Chronicles 24:13 confirms that the workmen wrought, and the work was perfected by them.

questions.question: What was made with the remaining money after the repairs according to 2 Chronicles 24:14?
options: Vessels for the house of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Vessels for the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 24:14 states that when they finished the work, they brought the rest of the money and made vessels for the house of the LORD.

questions.question: What happened to Jehoiada when he died according to 2 Chronicles 24:15?
options: He was buried among the kings
questions.correctAnswer: He was buried among the kings
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as stated in 2 Chronicles 24:16, where Jehoiada was buried in the city of David among the kings because he had done good in Israel.

questions.question: After Jehoiada's death, what did the princes of Judah do according to 2 Chronicles 24:17?
questions.explanation: According to 2 Chronicles 24:17, the princes of Judah made obeisance to the king after the death of Jehoiada.

questions.question: What did the people of Judah turn to after Jehoiada's death according to 2 Chronicles 24:18?
questions.explanation: This is confirmed in 2 Chronicles 24:18, which states that they left the house of the LORD and served groves and idols.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 24:2 suggest about Joash's reign while Jehoiada was alive?
questions.explanation: According to 2 Chronicles 24:2, Joash did that which was right in the sight of the LORD all the days of Jehoiada.

questions.question: Why did Joash gather the priests and Levites according to 2 Chronicles 24:5?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 24:5 states that Joash gathered the priests and Levites to collect money to repair the house of the LORD.

questions.question: What did Jehoiada do for Joash according to 2 Chronicles 24:3?
options: He took two wives for him
questions.correctAnswer: He took two wives for him
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 24:3, it is stated that Jehoiada took for Joash two wives, and he begat sons and daughters.

questions.question: Did the Levites hasten the collection as Joash commanded according to 2 Chronicles 24:5?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that the Levites hastened it not, which confirms that they did not comply with Joash's command.

questions.question: The statement 'Jehoiada waxed old and was full of days' is found in which verse?
questions.explanation: This statement is found in 2 Chronicles 24:15, affirming that Jehoiada was old and full of days when he died.

questions.question: The king ignored the Levites' duty according to 2 Chronicles 24:6.
questions.explanation: In fact, the king called for Jehoiada and asked why the Levites had not brought in the collection, indicating he was attentive to their duty.

questions.question: The people continued to worship the LORD after Jehoiada's death according to 2 Chronicles 24:18.
questions.explanation: After Jehoiada's death, the people left the house of the LORD and served groves and idols, indicating a turn away from worshiping the LORD.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 24 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 24.

questions.question: What did Joash do after the death of Jehoiada?
questions.explanation: After the death of Jehoiada, Joash hearkened to the princes of Judah and left the house of the LORD, serving groves and idols, as stated in 2 Chronicles 24:18.

questions.question: Who testified against the people, calling them back to the LORD?
questions.explanation: The Spirit of God came upon Zechariah, who stood above the people to deliver God's message, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 24:20.

questions.question: What was the fate of Zechariah after he testified against the people?
options: He was honored by the king
questions.explanation: The people conspired against Zechariah and stoned him at the command of the king, as stated in 2 Chronicles 24:21.

questions.question: What did Joash fail to remember that led to his downfall?
questions.explanation: Joash did not remember the kindness which Jehoiada had shown him, which is noted in 2 Chronicles 24:22.

questions.question: What did the army of Syria do to Judah and Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: The army of Syria came against Judah and Jerusalem, destroying the princes of the people, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 24:23.

questions.question: Why was Joash judged by the LORD?
questions.explanation: Joash was judged because he and the people forsook the LORD God of their fathers, as stated in 2 Chronicles 24:24.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'spirit' (רוּחַ, ruach) in 2 Chronicles 24:20 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'רוּחַ' (ruach) can mean wind, breath, or spirit, encompassing all mentioned meanings.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in 2 Chronicles 24:20 when Zechariah speaks?
questions.explanation: The message delivered by Zechariah features parallelism in the phrasing of transgressions and consequences, typical in Hebrew poetry.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of forsaking the LORD as seen in 2 Chronicles 24:18?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 2:13 speaks about forsaking God, paralleling the theme in 2 Chronicles 24:18 where the people left the house of the LORD.

questions.question: Which other passage fulfills the prophecy of judgment for forsaking God mentioned in 2 Chronicles 24:24?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:18 discusses God's wrath against those who forsake Him, echoing the judgment described in 2 Chronicles 24:24.

questions.question: What comes immediately before 2 Chronicles 24:25?
questions.explanation: Before the events of 2 Chronicles 24:25, Zechariah was stoned, leading to the subsequent conspiracy against Joash.

questions.question: What burden is mentioned in 2 Chronicles 24:27 regarding Joash?
questions.explanation: The verse notes the burdens laid upon him concerning his sons and the repairing of the house of God, as stated in 2 Chronicles 24:27.

questions.question: The army of the Syrians overcame Joash because of what reason as stated in 2 Chronicles 24:24?
questions.explanation: The LORD delivered a great host into the hands of the Syrians because Joash and the people had forsaken Him, as noted in 2 Chronicles 24:24.

questions.question: True or False: Joash was buried in the sepulchres of the kings.
questions.explanation: Joash was not buried in the sepulchres of the kings, as stated in 2 Chronicles 24:25.

questions.question: True or False: Zechariah was the son of Jehoiada the priest.
questions.explanation: Zechariah is explicitly mentioned as the son of Jehoiada the priest in 2 Chronicles 24:20.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 24 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 24 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 24:2 teach about human sanctification?
options: Human sanctification is dependent on faithful leadership.
Sanctification is solely an individual effort without external influence.
Sanctification is automatic once one becomes king.
Sanctification depends only on strict adherence to the law.
questions.correctAnswer: Human sanctification is dependent on faithful leadership.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 24:2 shows that Joash 'did that which was right... all the days of Jehoiada the priest,' indicating sanctification in the king was connected to Jehoiada's faithful priestly leadership.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 24:20 teach about divine judgment in relation to human sin?
options: God's judgment is a direct consequence of forsaking His commandments.
God ignores human sin if there is royal authority involved.
Divine judgment is random and unrelated to human actions.
Judgment is always delayed indefinitely regardless of sin.
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment is a direct consequence of forsaking His commandments.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 24:20 states that because the people 'have forsaken the LORD, he hath also forsaken you,' teaching that divine judgment is a direct response to human sin.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's providence is taught in 2 Chronicles 24:24 regarding national defeat?
options: God uses even a small enemy force to execute judgment when His people forsake Him.
Military success is always due to human strategy alone.
God never intervenes in political or military affairs.
Defeat comes only from numerical superiority of enemies.
questions.correctAnswer: God uses even a small enemy force to execute judgment when His people forsake Him.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 24:24 explains a small Syrian company defeated Judah because 'the LORD delivered a very great host into their hand,' showing God's providential control over national events.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 24:15 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 15 notes Jehoiada lived to 130 years and faithfully served, demonstrating God's longsuffering in preserving faithful servants over time.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 24:22 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: In verse 22, after Joash kills Zechariah, it says 'The LORD look upon it, and require it,' indicating God’s attribute of justice in holding accountable.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 24 prepare for the theme of covenant faithfulness in later prophetic books?
options: It illustrates the consequences of covenant unfaithfulness through judgment and calls to repentance.
It denies any connection between covenant faithfulness and national fate.
It teaches that God's covenant is unconditional regardless of human sin.
It focuses only on temple rituals without covenant implications.
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the consequences of covenant unfaithfulness through judgment and calls to repentance.
questions.explanation: Verses like 24:18-19 show Judah’s idolatry and God sending prophets, anticipating themes in prophetic books about covenant faithfulness and divine judgment.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does 2 Chronicles 24:4-14 have with the concept of temple restoration in the Old Testament?
options: It prefigures the ultimate restoration of God's presence in the Messiah.
It rejects the importance of temple worship in Israel’s religion.
It teaches that physical restoration of the temple is unnecessary for spiritual renewal.
It attributes temple restoration solely to human effort without divine involvement.
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the ultimate restoration of God's presence in the Messiah.
questions.explanation: The repair of the temple and continual offerings (24:4-14) points forward to the Messiah who fully restores God’s presence among His people.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 24:18 and 24:24 teach about the relationship between idolatry and divine judgment?
options: Idolatry provokes God’s wrath resulting in national defeat and judgment.
Idolatry is tolerated by God without consequences.
Divine judgment is unrelated to idolatry.
Idolatry leads to prosperity and divine favor.
questions.correctAnswer: Idolatry provokes God’s wrath resulting in national defeat and judgment.
questions.explanation: Verse 18 notes Judah’s idolatry causing wrath, and verse 24 records military defeat as divine judgment for forsaking God.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 24:20 and 24:21 teach about prophetic witness and rejection?
options: Prophetic messages from God often face rejection and result in the prophets’ suffering.
Prophets are always honored and accepted without opposition.
God never allows His prophets to suffer harm.
Prophetic words have no real impact on the people’s behavior.
questions.correctAnswer: Prophetic messages from God often face rejection and result in the prophets’ suffering.
questions.explanation: Verse 20 shows Zechariah’s prophetic rebuke, and verse 21 records his stoning, illustrating rejection and suffering of prophets.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 24:6 and 24:9 teach about covenant law and communal responsibility?
options: The law requires communal contributions to God’s house, emphasizing corporate responsibility.
Personal piety is sufficient without communal support of the temple.
The law forbids collecting money for temple repairs.
Only priests are responsible for temple maintenance.
questions.correctAnswer: The law requires communal contributions to God’s house, emphasizing corporate responsibility.
questions.explanation: Verse 6 references the commandment of Moses about collections, and verse 9 shows the proclamation for gathering contributions, indicating communal responsibility.

questions.question: Sceptics claim 2 Chronicles 24:22-25 teach that God condones royal violence and injustice. What does 2 Chronicles 24:22-25 actually teach?
options: God permits judgment on kings who commit injustice, signaling His condemnation of such acts.
God directly commands all royal violence as righteous.
The passage endorses the king’s actions without consequences.
Royal violence is celebrated as holy and justified.
questions.correctAnswer: God permits judgment on kings who commit injustice, signaling His condemnation of such acts.
questions.explanation: Verses 22-25 show Joash’s killing of Zechariah and subsequent judgment via disease, conspiracy, and dishonored burial, demonstrating divine condemnation of injustice.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 24:16 teach about the reward of faithful service to God in Israel?
options: Faithful servants are honored with burial among kings, signifying divine approval.
Faithful service is irrelevant to one’s honor after death.
Only kings receive honorable burial regardless of faithfulness.
God disregards human deeds when rewarding in death.
questions.correctAnswer: Faithful servants are honored with burial among kings, signifying divine approval.
questions.explanation: Verse 16 records Jehoiada’s burial among kings because 'he had done good in Israel,' linking faithful service with honor.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 24:19 specifically demonstrate in God’s response to Judah’s sin?
questions.explanation: Verse 19 shows God sending prophets repeatedly, demonstrating His faithfulness to call His people back despite their sin.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 24:23 and 24:25 teach about the consequences of covenant unfaithfulness for leadership and nation?
options: Unfaithfulness leads to military defeat, internal conspiracy, and dishonor for leaders and the nation.
Unfaithfulness results in immediate divine forgiveness without consequence.
Leaders remain unaffected by national sin and judgment.
Military success always follows covenant unfaithfulness.
questions.correctAnswer: Unfaithfulness leads to military defeat, internal conspiracy, and dishonor for leaders and the nation.
questions.explanation: Verse 23 describes Syrian defeat of Judah’s princes, and verse 25 shows Joash’s conspiracy and dishonored death, illustrating consequences of sin.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 24:5 teach about the nature of human responsibility in sanctification and temple upkeep?
options: Sanctification and temple upkeep require active, willing participation from the people.
Temple repair happens independently of human involvement.
Only kings are responsible for sanctification and temple repair.
Human responsibility is minimal and ineffective in spiritual matters.
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification and temple upkeep require active, willing participation from the people.
questions.explanation: Verse 5 records the king instructing priests and Levites to gather money yearly but the Levites 'hastened it not,' highlighting human responsibility.
